rules.statement: Property acquired by a wife during the subsistence of marriage for valuable consideration out of her separate estate is considered Thediathetam and not liable to be sold in execution of the husband's debts.
rules.supporting_quote: "The land in this case was purchased in the name of the wife with her dowry money. The marriage was after 1911 and the Thesawalamai Ordinance, No. 1 of 1911, applies. That Ordinance amends the previous law. Sections 21 and 22 govern this case. This property comes under 21 (a), i.e., property acquired for valuable consideration during the subsistence of the marriage."
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: "Property acquired for valuable consideration by either husband or wife during the subsistence of marriage"
